A superb performance 👏 https://t.co/MucWlTrgTY

And that’s that. Brighton were outstanding and here they recorded their biggest-ever win over rivals Crystal Palace after blitzing three goals in the first 10 minutes of the match. Hurzeler’s side are up to second in the league, for now, and have won six matches in a row.

"Would you look at that!" DIEGO GOMEZ SCORES FROM THE HALFWAY LINE! 🤯 https://t.co/qmagVbGEb4

Hurzeler said before this afternoon’s match that he wanted Brighton to be “ruthless” and here we are: Brighton are 5-0 up in the 92nd minute and still they want more.

De Cuyper bursts into the box, attacking the left half-space, and wins yet another Brighton corner. Yalcouye goes short again, but his eventual cross is easily gathered by Benitez.

Brighton are content to keep the ball here as the clock winds down. Passes across the backline prompt oles from the crowd, but with Palace sitting off, Hadjam senses an opening and bursts down the left, earning a corner for  his troubles.

Yalcouye plays short and the ball is worked to Hadjam on the edge of the box, but his searching ball goalwards is not up to much.

There will be four minutes of time added on.

“We want six,” sing the Brighton fans as Rutter earns another corner. It’s the same inswinging delivery that is played to the far post, this time it is Dunk who gets there, but his header across goal is cleared on this occasion.

Brighton 5 Crystal Palace 0 (Hinshelwood) Vuskovic and Dunk stalk up the pitch for another Brighton corner. And it’s the former who gets away from his marker Hughes to head goalwards off the inswinging delivery, and while Benitez keeps the defender’s effort out, Hinshelwood is there to finish from a yard out.

Jack Hinshelwood adds another for Brighton! 🔵 https://t.co/vpvAVURe0i

Sage makes his fifth and final substitution with Kamada making way for Hughes.

Boscagli and Ayari’s excellent afternoons are over as Hadjam and Yalcouye enter the field of play in their place.

Wharton tries to thread an ambitious ball over the top for Mateta to run on to, but it gets away from the Frenchman and Verbruggen gathers with ease.

There have been so many stand-out performances from players in blue and white, but how good as Vuskovic been this afternoon? Did not give Strand Larsen a sniff, made 11 defensive contributions and has progressed the ball whenever required.

Ayari tiptoes in off the left side, chopping inside Richards into a dangerous position, but the ball gets away from him and he’s unable to get a shot away before the chance disappears.

Chance! Palace come close to a consolation goal, Lerma rising highest at a corner but his header grazes the outside of the post and out for a goal-kick.

Nketiah fails to square to Mateta in front of Brighton’s goal moments later, but it is immaterial as he was offside anyhow.

Hurzeler makes his first substitutions of the match. Rutter and Hinshelwood, both of whom scored in midweek, are on in place of Kostoulas and Gross.

Lerma makes a meal out of a routine clearance, inadvertently tapping the ball with his left foot on to his right and out for a corner, much to the delight of the Brighton fans. Gross sends the ball in but puts too much on his delivery and it sails over everyone.

Canvot comes through the back of Kostoulas inside Palace’s half and gives away a foul. The free-kick is flighted into the box but Palace clear their lines on this occasion.

There seems to be a bit of needle emerging on the touchline as Crystal Palace coach Paddy McCarthy berates Brighton’s bench. He receives a yellow card for his troubles. Arguably the most intensity we’ve seen from the visitors all match.

Well that sums up Palace’s afternoon perfectly. It’s a terrible miss by Mateta, who has only just come on.

Nketiah combines nicely with McNeil in the left half-space before picking out the Frenchman in space inside the box, but his left-footed effort balloons on to the crossbar from a seemingly unmissable position. So, so poor.

More changes for Palace. Pino and Strand Larsen make way for Nketiah and Mateta.

One triumph of Brighton’s counter-pressing system is that they seemingly create “plus-one” situations across the entirety of the pitch. This cannot be the case, of course, but in the time it takes for Palace’s creators to pick out spaces, a Brighton marker is already on to them.

Lerma has replaced Ahanor as Sage looks to stem the tide. Brighton refuse to remove their foot from the pedal, though, and Gross spins in another free-kick, which is cleared, but only to Vuskovic on the edge of the box. The defender attempts to shape the ball into the top corner but makes too true of a contact and it sails well over.

Bournemouth 1 Sunderland 0 (Evanilson) The Brazilian pounces on a Sunderland error, dancing around Roefs and sliding the ball into an empty net.

Evanilson nets for the third game in a row 👏 https://t.co/t1DxRWVgYd

Brighton 4 Crystal Palace 0 (Kostoulas) This could get chalked off... There are two points of contention being scrutinised, a handball and an offside... But the goal stands! Gross was onside when he was played into the channel and Kostoulas is adjudged NOT to have handled the ball before sweeping in Brighton’s fourth goal of the afternoon.

Charalampos Kostoulas makes it FOUR for Brighton! 🔵 https://t.co/gUZLS3tWCx

Kamada has joined Wharton in the centre of the park with McNeil deployed just in advance of them.

But the change appears to have made no immediate impact as Vuskovic snaps into a strong tackle before continuing his run. In a wide-right position, he swings in a cross out to Kostoulas at the back post who drags his shot narrowly wide.

Sage makes a half-time change as Timber is replaced by McNeil.

Brighton have scored at least three goals in eight of their 11 matches this season.

51 - Diego Gómez's goal for Brighton against Crystal Palace was from 51 metres, the furthest range Premier League goal since Wayne Rooney for Everton v West Ham in November 2017 (58m). Incredible. https://t.co/Xm4lH1FLH7

Absolute domination. Muffled boos are heard from the away end as the referee brings the first half to a close. The Palace fans are still reeling after watching their side concede three times in the opening 10 minutes.

It’s really been a case of asphyxiation by counter-press for Palace here. Brighton have pounced on every loose touch and when they regain possession their forward players burst forth with further runners supporting underneath. It’s what they have been doing all season, but stopping it - even when you know it’s coming - is no easy feat.

There will be two minutes of time added on at the end of the first half.

It’s remarkable how easily Brighton are finding space between the lines, they’re pulling Palace’s markers to and fro, into and out of position.

Richards does get another go at tossing another throw-in back into the box, this time from the right, and Khalaili gets to this one, but heads well over.

Brighton utterly in control. They are dominating the ball and playing in a very controlled way, then bursting into life when Palace advance themselves.

Gomez has been fantastic this afternoon and he tiptoes his way past several Palace midfielders along the halfway line. Boscagli then has the presence of mind to switch the ball back out to the right and Gross’ set into the path of Kadioglu is struck goalwards and tipped behind by Benitez.

For the first time this afternoon, Mitchell makes a meaningful foray forward. He earns a throw-in near the corner flag which Richards launches into the box, but the ball slips out of his hands and Brighton clear their lines.

The resulting corner lands to Gross off the second phase but he cannot keep his effort down. He spins on his heels in frustration.

The hosts are letting Palace have the ball, settling into their defensive structure and funnelling the visitors around the outside, using the touchline as an extra defender to force errors.

Kadiologu works the ball infield from the right but cannot pick out Kostoulas. De Cuyper works the ball back into the middle for Ayari to strike goalwards from just outside the box, his effort takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner.

It’s taken Gross 30 minutes to make his first misstep. He goes into the book for a desperate tackle on Pino who had taken the ball away from the German with a superb first touch.

Close! A raking crossfield pass to Gomez at the far post is put back across the face of goal and a prone Ahanor is just about able to clear his lines. The young defender knew very little about that.

Brighton have complete control of the central areas, with Wharton and Timber struggling to get on top of their web of rotations and diversionary runs.

Palace win a free-kick 25 yards out and Pino, who has two goals in his last two outings, tries his luck but cannot clear the wall.

Brighton waste no time getting up the pitch and Kostoulas has a go from outside the box. His effort is straight at Benitez who gathers the ball at the second time of asking.

Danso is shown a red card as things go bad to worse for Sunderland at the Vitality. He brought down Evanilson as the Brazilian looked to be through on goal.

Finally some respite for Palace as Brighton choose to circulate the ball in front of their first line of pressure.

But back come the hosts soon after, De Cuyper bursting into the left of the box. This time Benitez is wise to the move and gets out smartly to cut it out.

Chants of “Are you Arsenal in disguise” ring out around the Amex...

This is utterly surreal. Gómez’s incredible strike had barely sunk in when Brighton harassed Palace again. This was a sumptuous team strike: a back heel from Kostoulas on the right setting up Ayari to tuck home. The atmosphere at Amex is electric. Brighton are heading second, below only Manchester City.

Brighton 3 Crystal Palace 0 (Gomez) Wow. Brighton are in dreamland here. Kostoulas finds space down the right and picks out the onrushing Ayari, whose effort beats Benitez via a Canvot deflection. That’s three goals in the first 10 minutes.

"Crystal Palace blown away here!" Brighton score a THIRD inside 10 minutes 🔥 https://t.co/YyoIw1zyaJ

Brighton 2 Crystal Palace 0 (Gomez) My goodness... That’s a goal-of-the-season contender, surely?! Wharton cedes possession on the halfway line and Gomez does the rest. He’s at most a yard inside Palace’s half and, spotting Benitez off his line, tries his luck from distance and finds the back of the net!

Goal of the season? From the halfway line, Diego Gómez picks up a loose ball and lobs Walter Benítez: shades of David Beckham at Wimbledon 30 years ago. Palace are in disarray.

"Would you look at that!" DIEGO GOMEZ SCORES FROM THE HALFWAY LINE! 🤯 https://t.co/qmagVbGEb4

Bournemouth 1 Sunderland 0 (Tavernier) A routine ball through the middle by Christie is not dealt with as Evanilson escapes the clutches of two defenders before squaring to Tavernier to finish.

Marcus Tavernier heads home his fourth goal of the season! 🍒 https://t.co/CI2pPjFw3I

Brighton 1 Crystal Palace 0 (Canvot OG) That’s superb from Gross. The German spins a delightful free-kick from the far side into the six-yard box and a retreating Canvot heads past his own goalkeeper.

Brighton only need three-and-a-half minutes to get their opener: a Pascal Gross free-kick from the left-hand side, headed into his own net by Palace centre-half Jaydee Canvot. Just the tonic for the thousands of Brighton fans being soaked.

Jaydee Canvot glances the ball into his own net and Brighton lead! 🔵 https://t.co/subm9ggwId

Kadioglu sets the tone early on, snapping in to cut off a loose pass out from the back by Palace. The ball is eventually worked up to Kostoulas, but he cannot bring it under his spell.

The heavens have opened up at the Amex, but that has not dampened the stadium announcer’s enthusiasm. He announces each player to the fans, with Pascal “the Goat” Gross’ name receiving an especially hearty cheer from the crowd.

The players (all 22 starters, it seems) take a knee before Brighton get us started.

The clouds have come in and the rain has started at the Amex as kick-off approaches. A raucous atmosphere, as you’d expect for the M23 derby, with plenty of Brighton fans relishing singing anti-Crystal Palace songs on the way to the ground. Should Brighton win - as they will expect to - they will move second, at least until Arsenal play later.

Kick-off is almost upon us. There’s just about enough time to make a brew before the action begins...

Eighteen-year-old defender Honest Ahanor starts in Palace’s back three alongside Jaydee Canvot, 20, and Chris Richards, 26. This afternoon will be a decent examination of their credentials as a unit. The Italy defender is on loan from Atalanta and will join Chelsea next summer.

The police-to-fan ratio looks fairly healthy here...

Palace fans head to #Brighton Station more on @brightonargus https://t.co/LQ9MKobmFH

Brighton’s form is all the more impressive given that Hurzeler has not had recourse to key men in Yankuba Minteh, Kaoru Mitoma and Mats Wieffer.

Femi Azeez, signed from Millwall in the summer for £15m, has only featured in a friendly match during the international break and remains sidelined with a muscle issue.

These missing men are nearing returns, and it makes you wonder whether Brighton can reach even further heights.

There will be supporters of both sides who are not particularly moved by this match-up. Some Crystal Palace fans may argue that their rivalry with Nottingham Forest has been more intense in recent years.

When asked about the rivalry, Sage said: “I know that the fans don’t like this name [the M23 derby] because it is too far to name it this. We know it is a big game for the club and the fans, and we have to show our better phases, like the second halves of our last two games.”

Interestingly, the categories in which Brighton have excelled marry up almost perfectly with Crystal Palace’s weakest areas. Here are their numbers in the same/reciprocal departments:

Brighton’s fast start to the season has been evidenced by league-leading numbers in key departments, particularly in the attacking third.

"I have to give a lot of credit to my players" Fabian Hürzeler discusses Brighton's blistering start to the season 👏 https://t.co/o92tBqBO9i

What is it? Well, I have been reliably advised that this is a take on a social media trend where implausible, dystopian AI videos are set to the song Storm II by GENER8ION featuring Yung Lean (don’t worry, me neither).

While some may argue that Palace’s roller-coaster 2025-26 season was at times dystopian (just ask Marc Guéhi or Oliver Glasner), the Europa League trophy is very much real. No AI needed here.

Pascal previews today's test... 💬 https://t.co/Cgj4APvfi4

"We have to play with passion and energy" Régis Le Bris speaks ahead of Sunderland's visit to Bournemouth 🎙️ https://t.co/KgWfOi4Pt5

Palace have conceded in the first 20 minutes of three of their six league games this season, and within the first 10 minutes in their last two outings.

It is a concern Sage acknowledged in his pre-match press conference: “It’s difficult to explain… We just have to put altogether the conditions to start well to make a good game in the whole of this one [against Brighton]. I think we are able to do it, we did it in Leeds, now we are in this situation.

“We are aware of what’s happened in these two games [against Forest and Lyon], one was a good result, one was a bad result, but in each game, when we are 100 per cent on what we have to do in our gameplan, I think we are able to do really wonderful things. When we are not like this, it is another story.”

Brighton have played against 10 men twice this season but were consigned to that very fate last weekend at the Stadium of Light.

Having gone ahead through De Cuyper, Struijk was given his marching orders (a decision that has since been overturned on appeal) and the visitors were made to show a different side to their character, battling in a deep block and frustrating Sunderland before adding a second.

"Today it's up to us" Marco Rose is hoping for Bournemouth's first league win of the season 🍒 https://t.co/VoNR9VfCOd

Pascal Gross may be 35 years old, but he is enjoying one of the finest seasons of his career, creating the most chances in the Premier League. Of his midfield talisman, Hurzeler said: “It started in pre-season. During pre-season he’s never the person who can lay on the beach for several hours doing nothing…

“He really suffered in pre-season. In pre-season you really build a foundation for the whole season, you build a physical foundation, a resilience, you build also the mindset… How he came back after this break was impressive. He looked so fit, so sharp, so ready… We saw a different face from him already and then it’s just a progression for him on the pitch…

“Of course no one expected it would be that good, but shows that he still has all this capacity in his body.”

Neither Brobbey nor Isidor make the match-day squad, so it will be up to 21-year-old Tutyerov to lead the line for Sunderland.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the M23 derby – or El Gatwicko, as the kids call it these days – as high-flying Brighton and Hove Albion host Crystal Palace at the Amex Stadium. Being frank, this is neither the fiercest nor the most storied Premier League rivalry, but few would have imagined when these sides faced off in the Third Division in the mid-1970s that this would ever become a top-flight match-up sandwiched between European games.

Brighton have been outstanding this season and took their league form into the Conference League, thrashing Lithuanian champions Kauno Zalgiris on Thursday night. Fabian Hürzeler was delighted by his fringe players’ performances on Thursday night and may have some selection questions to answer with Jack Hinshelwood and Georginio Rutter finding the net. Brighton are third in the Premier League and were the division’s heaviest scorers after the last round of matches.

Yet the Palace nut has been a tough one to crack for Hürzeler, having not yet registered a win in four attempts. When asked what he enjoyed most about the rivalry, the German said: “Nothing yet, because I didn’t win any games so far. Hopefully on Sunday this changes… I like these games because they’re derbies, more emotions, it’s a rivalry, it’s [us] against Crystal Palace.”

In his pre-match interview Hürzeler admitted to being an admirer of Pierre Sage, and while the Frenchman’s side have failed to match Brighton’s fast start, they rallied impressively to defeat rivals Nottingham Forest last weekend and fought back valiantly away at Lyon, albeit in a losing effort, in midweek. The return of Ismaïla Sarr from injury is a significant boost.

Elsewhere Bournemouth host Sunderland hoping to secure their first Premier League victory of the season. Marco Rose’s side and Tottenham are the only teams still without a win, but Bournemouth have been perfect in the Europa League and will look to transfer some of that momentum into the league. Sunderland scored late to win away at Portuguese side Torreense.

You can also follow the latest updates from Manchester United’s crucial trip to Elland Road in our sister blog here.

#1380. Mitochondrial protein import defects enhance tumour immunogenicity

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

Tumour cells evade detection and elimination by the immune system through a suite of adaptations1, including the repression of antigen presentation, which is required for the recognition of tumour cells by CD8+ T cells. Mitochondria have emerged as targets for enhancing antitumour immunity; however, the extensive mitochondrial proteome has remained largely unstudied for its ability to modulate immune responses. Here we show that defects in the mitochondrial protein import machinery promote tumour immunogenicity and synergize with immune checkpoint blockade treatment in melanoma models. Mitochondrial protein import perturbation, specifically through depletion of the TIM23 import complex subunit TIMM50, enhances tumour immunogenicity through a pathway involving mitochondrial DNA escape, cGAS–STING pathway activation and interferon-β (IFNβ) secretion. Secreted IFNβ signals through the type I IFN receptor to activate the JAK–STAT pathway, resulting in increased antigen presentation on MHC class I complexes. Mitochondrial DNA escape in Timm50-depleted cells is linked to the formation of mitochondrial-derived vesicles. Depletion of SNX9 and RAB9, involved in mitochondrial-derived vesicle formation2, suppresses mitochondrial DNA-dependent type I IFN production and signalling. By disrupting mitochondrial proteostasis and membrane architecture, defective protein import in Timm50-depleted cells drives the immune phenotype. This study shows that mitochondrial protein import inhibition causes tumour immunogenicity, including sensitization to immune checkpoint blockade, by promoting mitochondrial DNA escape and IFNβ-driven MHC class I antigen presentation.

#1379. Everton Women Welcome JYSK As Official Home Furnishing Retail Partner

Everton Women has announced a new partnership with international home furnishing retailer JYSK, which will become the Club's ‘Official Home Furnishing Retail Partner’.

The agreement brings together Everton and the Danish retailer, renowned for its Scandinavian-inspired furniture and homeware, in a partnership that will enhance facilities at Goodison Park and support community initiatives across Merseyside.

JYSK (pronounced 'YOOSK') operates more than 3,600 stores worldwide, with a presence in the Liverpool City Region through its outlets in Hunts Cross and St Helens. The Scandinavian retailer will provide furniture and homeware to create welcoming spaces for players, staff and supporters at Goodison Park.

The announcement marks Everton Women's third dedicated commercial partnership, following agreements with GGM Gastro and, most recently, Nestlé Confectionery, further demonstrating the growing appeal of the Club to leading international businesses.

Everton Women's move to Goodison Park has provided a distinctive platform for commercial growth, combining the Club's rich footballing heritage with new opportunities for partners to play a meaningful role in the future of women's football.

JYSK will also support the work of Everton in the Community, with furniture featured in the partnership's launch campaign donated to the charity's 'Home Is Where The Heart Is' programme, which supports young adults experiencing or at risk of homelessness.

The donated items will make a valuable contribution to the charity's four-bedroom residential property in the L4 area of Liverpool, further enhancing the welcoming and supportive environment provided for young people as they develop the skills and confidence needed to live independently.

Andrew Middleton, President of Business Operations at Everton, said: "We're delighted to welcome JYSK to Everton Women. There's a natural connection between a business that helps people make a house a home and the next chapter we're creating at Goodison Park, and we're looking forward to bringing that to life for our players and supporters.

"What particularly stands out is JYSK's commitment to making a positive difference beyond football. Their support for Everton in the Community is a fantastic example of how we want our partnerships to deliver meaningful benefits, both for the Club and the communities we represent.

"There's a growing recognition among businesses of the opportunities around Everton Women, and we're focused on building partnerships that go beyond traditional sponsorship. JYSK is another great addition to that journey and we're excited about what we can achieve together."

Roni Tuominen, Country Director, JYSK Ireland & UK, said: "Everton Women has an incredible story with a rich heritage and community roots. The team has made a positive start to the season and we can’t wait to support them at Goodison Park and help turn this legacy stadium into a home."

JYSK's partnership will be visible at Goodison Park for the first time when Everton Women host Durham Women in the Subway Players Cup on Wednesday 11 November (7pm GMT kick-off), with branding featuring on the stadium's big screens and pitchside LED advertising.

To celebrate the announcement, JYSK will also give away limited-edition JYSK x Everton tote bags at its Hunts Cross Retail Park store on Saturday 14 and Sunday 15 November.

The bags will be available to customers making a purchase, with no minimum spend, on a first-come, first-served basis while stocks last.

For more information about JYSK, visit jysk.co.uk.

#1378. The little-known new face called up by England: Can you name the star brought in to replace Ezri Konsa?

Published: 05:58 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 12:26 EST, 10 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel has made a first-time England call-up to replace Ezri Konsa - but casual fans could be forgiven if they do not recognise the latest Three Lions addition.

He is not a widely-recognised face among the stars from the Premier League and other top European leagues in Tuchel's selection but James Hill, 24, has starred for Bournemouth in their eight-match winning run under Marco Rose this season.

The central defender, who started his career at Fleetwood Town, has enjoyed a dream few months: He married partner Tara Rose in June, welcomed his first child in August and has now had his maiden England call.

England announced today that Arsenal defender Konsa will not be in contention to face Croatia at Wembley on Thursday night - although he will be fit to potentially face Spain away on Sunday - and Hill has been called up in his place.

Hill has played for England's Under 20s and Under 21s but this is his first senior call. He was signed by Bournemouth for just £1.2million in 2022 - beating Sheffield United, Burnley, Leeds, Southampton, Tottenham and even Barcelona, who all checked on his progress.

Bournemouth's official X account posted today: 'Congratulations, Hilly. Our defender has earned a first senior @England call-up.'

James Hill - pictured with new wife Tara - has been called up to the latest England squad (Source: Instagram/james_hill_10)

Hill has starred for Bournemouth in their eight-match winning run under Marco Rose

Hill's route to the top is a fascinating one. He attended a trial day at Fleetwood as a 14-year-old and managed to impress them enough to earn place at their new academy.

Interestingly, Hill did not play for a football team of any kind before he was 10, simply kicking a ball around with friends and playing in the garden to hone his skills.

Blackpool opted against signing him after a trial and he was then dropped by Bolton after a short stint.

It proved to be a shrewd piece of talent identification from Fleetwood, with Hill later becoming the club's record sale, eclipsing the fee they received for Jamie Vardy.

And having signed for the Cherries in 2022, Hill has now established himself as a key member of Marco Rose's side.

He's played every minute of every Premier League match this season at the heart of the defence and clearly Tuchel has been impressed.

Speaking before his call-up, Hill said: 'It’s every kid’s dream, isn’t it? You grow up watching the Three Lions on TV, for the World Cup, the Euros. It’s one of the greatest honours you can have in football.'

Football is in the blood for Hill. His father, Matt, made more than 550 appearances in the Football League for the likes of Preston North End, Wolverhampton Wanderers, Sheffield United and Queens Park Rangers as a defender.

Hill played for England at age group level, pictured here kissing his now wife after a game

Hill's younger brother, Tyler, is also in the game, playing for Torquay United in National League South.

But Matt did not pressure his sons into the sport, with James previously telling the Times: 'He didn’t want me to feel as though it’s a job.

'He wanted me to feel like I’m wanting to be here because I love doing it. This is my passion. It brings me happiness. He wanted me to come to that conclusion, not for him to make that decision for me.'

Hill was a well-rounded sportsman and his secondary school did not even play football. Instead, he excelled as a fly-half for the rugby side and impressed as a javelin thrower.

He attributes his success as being aided by trying his hand at different disciplines and it is paying off in abundance having had to largely bide his time before earning a first-team spot under Andoni Iraola last term, with loans to Blackburn and Hearts helping him develop.

Hill's progress flew somewhat under the radar somewhat for many fans outside of Bournemouth and his career peak of an England call-up coincides with domestic bliss.

Having married Tara in the summer, they welcomed their daughter Edie two months later.

Hill, pictured, heading the ball away against Ipswich has become one of the best defenders in the Premier League

'Becoming a dad is one of the most special things I’ve ever experienced in my life,' he said. 'There isn’t a manual though, it’s just like, "Congratulations, you’ve got a baby". Then the door shuts! Hang on a minute. What am I supposed to do next? Is there a book for this? My wife has been absolutely incredible.'

He regularly shares pictures from both his professional and personal life on social media, putting wedding snaps alongside action shots of Bournemouth games.

Hill's England call-up will no doubt introduce him to a whole new audience previously unaware of the defender's capabilities, with only 34,000 Instagram followers at present.

The 24-year-old must now impress Tuchel enough to earn some game time when England play Croatia on Thursday in their next Nations League encounter.

#1377. Hearts boss Vrancken is playing with fire by turning the guns on his own players

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 12:17 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 12:26 EST, 10 November 2026

Not for the first time this season under Wouter Vrancken, Hearts suffered a complete and utter implosion as they were thrashed 5-2 at home to Falkirk last weekend.

This is a team who lost 6-0 to Sturm Graz over two legs in the Champions League qualifiers back at the start of the campaign.

A team who were then battered 6-1 away against Benfica in Lisbon in the Europa League qualifiers – and a team who were also thumped 7-1 against Celtic at Parkhead a few weeks ago.

Hearts also lost the derby to Hibs just over a week ago in the semi-finals of the Premier Sports Cup at Hampden.

Now comes an annihilation against Falkirk where Hearts were 4-0 down by half-time. What a shambolic way to lose a long unbeaten record at home.

Even accounting for what had gone before in some of those matches this season, what happened on Sunday at Tynecastle felt like a new low.

Hearts were a shambles. But what was even more alarming was the manager's inability to stop the bleeding and make any changes from the touchline.

All of which poses a very simple question. Have Hearts and Jamestown made a mistake with Vrancken? At the moment, he looks hopelessly one-dimensional.

But it was his post-match comments on Sunday afternoon which actually became even more alarming than the performance itself.

Wouter Vrancken was 'embarrassed' by Hearts' 5-2 home loss to Falkirk

Vrancken branded it 'embarrassing' and a 'disgrace'. He called his players 'childish' and basically insinuated that they lacked any spirit or character until the youngsters came off the bench.

In the midst of a horrendous injury crisis and with players dropping like flies, that is a very dangerous game for any manager to play. He threw them under a bus.

By publicly slaughtering his players like that during a time of adversity and when many of them are being asked to play out of position, he is playing with fire.

Those are the type of comments that could very easily lose a dressing room. His comments would have gone down like a lead balloon among the squad.

Hearts have had the best part of a dozen players missing through injury. Vrancken himself has branded it an injury crisis unlike any other he has experienced throughout his career.

But what is most curious in all of this is that Vrancken seems totally unwilling to engage in any self-reflection throughout all of this.

After the shellacking at Celtic Park a few weeks ago, he lamented the fact his team had made too many individual errors.

There was no acknowledgment that his system had set them up to fail. No acceptance that pressing Celtic man-for-man and leaving players one-v-one at the back was a huge part of the problem.

Since he arrived in the summer, Vrancken's preferred style of play has been front-foot attacking football. There have been times when it has clicked reasonably well.

When he had his key players fit, Hearts were a good watch. But when the guts of a full team were then ripped out due to injury, it has quickly disintegrated into chaos.

Continuing to demand the same high-pressing and attacking style of play without meaningful adjustment is not principled. It is naive, inflexible, and tactically illiterate.

When the structure collapses, as it did against Falkirk and in the 7-1 defeat at Celtic, the emphasis returns to individual mistakes rather than collective vulnerability created by the system itself.

It is a classic example of a manager publicly hanging his players out to dry rather than choosing to accept his own part in the wider failings.

Hearts are not in crisis yet. They still sit fourth in the table, just a point behind Falkirk. But this is a team who have clearly regressed from where they were last season.

Vrancken was hired on the basis that he could bring a more dynamic style of play and move the team forward from the platform left behind by Derek McInnes.

As written in these pages a few weeks ago after the defeat to Celtic, there is absolutely no prospect whatsoever of this Hearts team challenging for the title this time around.

The current combination of a horrendous injury list, a rigid tactical approach and increasingly pointed public criticism of the players is a dangerous mixture that threatens to undermine everything.

Scottish football's fixture congestion, the demands of European competition and the physical toll of the season have exposed the limits of Vrancken's one-dimensional plan.

Adaptation is not a betrayal of principles. It is a basic requirement of the job when circumstances change this dramatically.

The international break offers a brief window. A handful of bodies may return for Hearts' next fixture against Dundee at Dens Park.

The more important return would be a change in tone and a willingness to adapt the demands placed on those players left still standing.

Publicly branding his players as 'a disgrace' while refusing to acknowledge that the system itself is contributing to their vulnerability is a sure-fire way to get himself sacked.

Vrancken's Hearts squad has been ravaged by injuries this season

The manager is entitled to be angry. He is entitled to demand better. He is not entitled to ignore the context he is operating in or the effect his words will have on a group already stretched to breaking point.

Vrancken arrived with a clear identity and early promise. The test now is whether he can evolve that identity under pressure or whether he remains locked into one way of playing regardless of the resources available.

Hearts cannot afford the latter. Much more of this public slaughtering and the players will switch off. Vrancken will have lost them completely.

Players will run for a manager who shows understanding of their situation even while criticising their standards.

They will begin to switch off for one who appears to place the preservation of his methods above the protection of the group.

That is the risk Vrancken is running. It is a risk no manager in the middle of a crippling injury crisis can afford to take.

#1375. Slow and dull Man Utd are just not good enough

Manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet. You fix one problem – being far too vulnerable to conceding goals – only to create another – lacking the threat to score. It is all very Meh United not Man United. The indisputable fact is they are just not very entertaining to watch. They are slow and dull.

In the end it also points to another thing. The thing highlighted in midweek by Lisandro Martínez after the Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid: they do not have the strength in depth to compete.

What they do have appears to not be fit for purpose. Certainly Michael Carrick, the under-pressure manager, is struggling to get the best out of the resources he has.

“It’s like a duvet,” Toshack, the former Real Madrid and Wales manager, famously said of football. “If you pull it up, your feet get cold. If you pull it down, your shoulders get cold.”

There will have been times in the last few days, with the intense criticism and scrutiny over his future, when Carrick will have simply felt like dragging that duvet up over his head and keeping it there.

Defeat by Leeds United would have been unthinkable. It would have put Carrick under potentially intolerable pressure in what appears to be a pivotal week, with Como away in the Champions League and a home Premier League fixture against Bournemouth in the coming days.

Was this a lifeline or the tightening of the noose for Carrick? Time will soon tell. The relief of avoiding defeat was tempered by the reality of it now being just one win in their opening seven league games – at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town – and they are down in 13th place. It is six games without a win in all competitions.

That is unacceptable and is their fewest number of league victories in a top-flight campaign since 1986-87. Back then they sacked their manager in November and brought in a certain Alex Ferguson.

The hard truth is Carrick needs to start collecting some “Ws” in those results columns. United are already 14 points behind leaders Manchester City and five outside the probable Champions League places. Qualifying again for that tournament must be the minimum expectation.

Ruben Amorim, Carrick’s predecessor, lost his job within 24 hours of the same 1-1 scoreline at Elland Road last season – dismissed after Martínez-like explosive comments again aimed at director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick will not suffer the same fate after this, but the ice is becoming increasingly thin.

We have seen this movie before at United. A slow start to the season, a period of drift, falling out of contention, no reaction on the pitch, backing from the hierarchy that becomes increasingly unconvincing. And then a change.

Can Carrick, who genuinely does still retain support at the highest level, alter that pattern? Does he have it in him? Is he too passive like his team? Carrick said this draw felt like a “fresh start”, but on this evidence that comment can be classified as wildly optimistic.

Having directed his criticism at the United hierarchy, and specifically Wilcox, the former Leeds winger who was here, over a lack of summer signings, Martínez apologised and was named in the starting XI. But the Argentine only lasted to half-time, withdrawn injured with a tight thigh, and sat watching the second half with his hood up over his head.

What United did sign in the last window was three midfielders – at a cost of £155m – and all three started: Carlos Baleba alongside Andrey Santos with Youri Tielemans in the No 10 role, which meant Bruno Fernandes was pushed out to the left, from where he constantly wanted to come in-field, with Amad Diallo on the right.

Carrick talked of having a “fresh spine” as well as that fresh start. But it did not make for a potent combination even if, further forward, Bryan Mbeumo played through the middle and scored one. He should have scored another.

Bryan Mbeumo finds the net this time to put Manchester United 1-0 up at Leeds! 🔴 https://t.co/NKDIhlUND1

But beyond that United created little. “It was a dominant performance against Man United,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, claimed. He was right. If one team deserved to win it was his. They had the chances but snatched at them with Anton Stach, in injury time, having a weak shot cleared off the line by Martínez’s replacement Noussair Mazraoui after a mistake by goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Stach had to score.

United were ahead at half-time. Mbeumo had headed wastefully wide when unmarked but did well to force his way past James Justin and meet a low cross from Tielemans to poke the ball home. The way the usually undemonstrative Carrick punched the air in his technical area showed the pressure he felt. It was something to build on. To gain control.

Leeds had started well but did not really pose much of a threat – beyond forcing Lammens to save well from Nico Elvedi’s downward header – and maybe the earlier kick-off subdued the crowd. This was far from a bear pit.

But after the break, Leeds were comfortably the better side. The nature of their equalising goal, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin too strong and alert for first Baleba and then Mbeumo to fire in from a corner, exposed the enduring softness at the heart of United.

Michael Carrick says he has put on “the headphones” this week in an effort to drown out the noise, but admitted Manchester United have to stop their struggles from snowballing.

United sit just two points above the relegation zone after a 1-1 draw at Leeds left them with just one win from their opening seven Premier League matches.

Carrick claimed the result felt like a “fresh start” after a week in which Lisandro Martínez publicly apologised for criticising Jason Wilcox, the United director of football, and the Old Trafford board.

But the United manager acknowledged their position “doesn’t look too good” and that they must start winning soon to stop the club from entering another doom cycle.

“Listen, we’re not accepting it as everything’s great by any stretch, so I’m realistic with that,” said the United manager, who claimed “the headphones have been on this week”.

“But sometimes you do struggle, sometimes there’s a bit of it where you have to find a way through it. We haven’t really had to go through that yet [before now] and we have to find a way through it.

“There has been a cycle at times here over a period of time when it can go in different directions. We’ve got to be stable enough to keep doing the right things for the right reasons as a group, and we’re more than capable of winning football matches.

“I understand the situation doesn’t look too good if you look at it from a certain way, but I’ve no doubts we can go on a good run.”

United face Como in the Champions League in Italy on Wednesday before Bournemouth visit Old Trafford four days later.

Carrick said he remains convinced United can still have a strong campaign, despite their worst start to a season for 40 years. I know what we’ve got in the changing room, where we want to get to, how we want to get there,” he said. “We know we can do it.

“We’ve done it for some time, and we feel we’re a better group now, and I do feel that. Sometimes it doesn’t always show, but you get a feeling and I’m encouraged by a lot of things. And if we keep doing the right things, I think we can still have a really good season.”

Asked if he would be putting the headphones back on this week ahead of two more pivotal games, Carrick added: “Nah, it’s always quiet for me.”

Martínez was substituted at half-time at Elland Road with a tight thigh just days after his tirade at club executives and Marcus Rashford was left out for “purely tactical” reasons. “Nothing personal, the front players were doing a good job on and off the ball,” Carrick said. “Everyone is ready for Wednesday.”

The Leeds boss told Sky Sports: “We are slightly disappointed it is just a point. Overall, I felt it was not necessary to be losing at half time but it is still Manchester United. Second half, we got the equaliser, we should have kept up the dominance, too many strikes went over the crossbar but it was overall a solid performance. We should have won the game but we move on.

“We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month if we were seen as favourites against Manchester Untiedbut we have earned this. We wanted to prove the comments right.

“We were the dominant side but we couldn’t capitalise as we lacked quality in and around the box.

“It says a lot about how much respect we have earned. Overall, this is where we are at the moment and overall, it is a good place to be.

“It is still difficult in this league to win points. You have to be clinical and be very, very effective but we have to keep going.”

Speaking to Sky Sports, he said: “I think we could’ve played with a bit more quality in the final third, particularly in the first half. We were getting good quality in the box but just not enough numbers.

“We made sure in the second half we came out with more confidence going forward. I think we were unlucky not to win the game.

“They tried to [match us up formation-wise]. Not surprised given what happened last season. They were probably looking at our physical output and the way we liked to play and tried to go man-for-man.

Just 10 months on from Ruben Amorim’s final game in charge of Manchester United, the club return to Elland Road on Sunday afternoon with another manager under pressure and the director of football again in the spotlight.

The difference is Michael Carrick still has a chance to determine the course of his United future whereas Amorim had already sealed his fate after a furious bust-up with Jason Wilcox 48 hours before his last game ended in a 1-1 draw with Leeds and post-match fireworks.

But even for a club never far from a crisis, it seems remarkable to think they are back in a tailspin so soon after Amorim’s sacking in early January.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Leeds United at Elland Road.

Quiet week in the world of Man Utd? Don’t be silly. Following a 2-0 defeat in the Champions League against Atlético Madrid in Spain on Wednesday, defender Lisandro Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on Man Utd’s director of football Jason Wilcox and the club’s hierarchy because of a dreadful start to the campaign, which has yielded two victories in nine games across all competitions.

The Argentine criticised Man Utd’s recruitment and said he expected more, but didn’t suggest Carrick was to blame. Martinez has since apologised for his outburst and met with Wilcox, Man Utd chief executive Omar Berrada and Michael Carrick, with Telegraph Sport understanding that he’s free to play today, although his role remains unclear as we all eagerly await the team news.

Carrick is under immense pressure to get a result here in Yorkshire, with last weekend’s 1-1 draw with 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford condemning Man Utd to their worst league start for 40 years.

With all eyes on the visitors, Leeds will be licking their lips at the prospect of piling further misery on their beleaguered opponents. Daniel Farke’s side suffered their first Premier League loss last weekend, falling 2-1 to Arsenal at the Emirates after going a goal up, but the mood remains positive after a solid start to the campaign.

Leeds are eighth and the club will be harbouring ambitions of a top-half finish in the Premier League for the first time since the 2019/20 season, with the prospect of qualifying for European football not out of the realm of possibility.

Unlike Man Utd, Leeds have a settled, reliable system that clearly suits their current squad. Elland Road will also be a cauldron of hostility and noise, given the fierce backdrop between these two bitter rivals.

This has all the ingredients to be a thrilling and fascinating watch as we bring you the latest updates, information and drama. Kick-off is at 14:00, with team news coming shortly.
