Some excellent, if disquieting, detail from Sam Dean in this piece about the mood around Arsenal away from the first-team following the news of 60 planned redundancies. Sam writes that there are expecting to be other experienced and influential figures departing. The timing of cuts invites particular scrutiny, coming after the emotional peak of winning the league, record revenues and Mikel Arteta’s new contract.

After Arsenal were beaten by Bayern Munich in a Champions League quarter-final two years ago, Mikel Arteta bemoaned a lack of “magic moments” in attack.

Arsenal have since progressed to a Champions League semi-final and final, while ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title.

The upward trajectory has translated to tangible success, but Arsenal are still searching the level-raising attacker they lacked on their last visit to the Allianz Arena in 2024.

Back then, Arsenal’s offensive game revolved around Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard and that remains the case, which makes one wonder if Arsenal’s forward options have been adequately renewed.

A pair of stodgy performances (in victory) against Leeds United and Nottingham Forest have amplified those questions, though some of Arsenal’s slicker football in the season’s early weeks has been forgotten a little hastily.

They have made another strong start to another European campaign with six points from six, but this is undoubtedly their hardest fixture of the league phase.

Their chances of matching last season’s eight wins from eight could well hinge on the outcome of tonight’s game, but there are worse times to face Bayern.

Vincent Kompany’s team looks as formidable as ever, having scored 22 goals from six Bundesliga games so far this season. Their rotational approach is hard to track, with runners from deep breaking beyond Harry Kane who wanders into deep midfield positions.

However, they are without Michael Olise (suspension) and Jamal Musiala (injury) while Joshua Kimmich will miss the game on compassionate grounds following the death of his father.

With the exception of William Saliba, Christos Tzolis and Piero Hincacpie, Arsenal have a pretty clean bill of health and the strength of their bench was crucial against Leeds, Lille and Forest last week.

For Arteta, there are some interesting selection calls to make. It is anticipated that Jurrien Timber will replace Ben White at right-back, and first-choice left-back Riccardo Calafiori has been rested for the Champions League games so far. Should Arteta continue that policy, Myles Lewis-Skelly will fill the position, which will likely mean a midfield start for Bruno Guimarães or Mikel Merino.

Arsenal’s manager must also decide between Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze on the left, and Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front. Havertz is Arteta’s preference, but he also has to consider a relatively short turnaround before Saturday’s league game against Everton.

#1346. Momiki Hat-Trick Sees Blues Thrash Durham

Yuka Momiki’s second-half hat-trick helped Everton make it four wins from four in the Subway Players Cup with an impressive 6-0 win against Durham.

The 30-year-old came on at half-time and netted a fine trio of goals, with a brace from Noemie Mouchon and a first goal for Everton for Jutta Rantala completing the scoring for the dominant Toffees.

The Blues set the tone for the evening as Mouchon rifled an effort in to the palms of Cat Sheppard within the opening minute.

Rantala then followed that up with a venomous strike of her own two minutes later as the keeper was called in to action once more.

The Finland international, who celebrated her birthday on Tuesday, came even closer on 9 minutes as her rising shot rattled the crossbar.

It was Rantala who then opened the scoring on 20 minutes as her persistence paid off. Hannah Cain pulled an enticing ball across the face of goal. Fellow forward Rantala brought it down before unleashing an unstoppable effort in to the top right corner to net her first goal in royal blue.

The hosts continued to control the tempo throughout the opening 45 – probing their opponents and boasting the clear majority of possession and chances.

At the break, Phelan made a double change as Rosa van Gool, Maz Pacheco and Momiki replaced Wheeler, Kitagawa and Vignola.

Those substitutes immediately paid off as Momiki fired home at the Gwladys Street End five minutes after the interval. Upon reaching the penalty spot, Everton’s number 29 elegantly placed the ball in to the bottom right corner.

That corner was found by the ball again on 64 minutes as Mouchon finished past the diving keeper. The French forward brought the ball down excellently – it almost sticking to her right foot. She then pulled the trigger early, slotting past the outrushed Sheppard.

One minute later, Plano came on for her Everton debut to mark another memorable evening for the Club’s Academy.

Momiki then doubled her tally in the 70th minute with the best of her three strikes. From the edge of the box, she curled in to the far corner. The Gwladys rose, with Momiki’s appreciation for the iconic stand reciprocated by the Evertonians’ cheers.

With five minutes remaining, Mouchon secured a brace of her own. The forward saw an initial strike saved, but prodded home the rebound to cap off a rapid break.

The loudest cheer of the night occurred only a single minute later as Momiki secured the match ball to conclude a brilliant evening to be a Blue.

#1345. A Yeboah back in the Premier League? Leeds legend Tony's nephew Kelvin wanted by several clubs in January transfer window after scoring 18 goals in MLS for Minnesota United this term

Published: 04:00 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 04:36 EST, 11 November 2026

Another goal-packed season for Kelvin Yeboah in Major League Soccer (MLS) is expected to spark interest among Premier League and Championship clubs in January.

Yeboah has ended the campaign with 18 goals and made five assists for Minnesota United who finished 10th of 15 teams in the Western Conference, just one point outside and one place outside the play-offs.

It means the season is over for the 26-year-old nephew of Leeds legend Tony Yeboah.

Yeboah describes himself as 'more of a modern nine' than his uncle Tony, who was famed for his muscular physique and his ability to strike with ferocious volleys from distance. He is sharp and mobile with a goal instinct.

Premier League and Championship clubs have been monitoring his progress this season.

Everton and Crystal Palace, both in search of firepower and options up front, are among those who have been linked to a move. Free-spending Ipswich are another.

Kelvin Yeboah is wanted by many Premier League goals after a fine goalscoring season in MLS

Yeboah scored 18 goals for Minnesota United - with Everton, Crystal Palace and Ipswich keen

The striker is the 26-year-old nephew of Tony Yeboah, a Leeds United legend of the mid-1990s

There is interest also from Europe. Hoffenheim boss Christian Ilzer signed Yeboah when in charge of Sturm Graz, after the young forward had scored four goals against his Austria Vienna team in a cup tie in the previous season.

Yeboah has been in Minnesota since the summer of 2024. There is another season on his contract and the option of one more after that.

But he remains keen to test himself at the top of the European game and there is a growing feeling that he could be on the move in the next window.

'As a footballer, you want to play on the biggest stages and express who you are as a person,' he told Daily Mail Sport in an interview on the eve of the MLS season. 'I just want to keep scoring goals and give myself the best chance of that happening.'

He grew up in Italy from the age of three to 15 and represented the Azzurri at Under-21 level. He is also eligible for Ghana where he was born.

At 15, he moved to London where he played non-league football for AC London and had trials at several clubs including West Ham before joining WSG Tirol in Austria at the age of 18.

Yeboah scored 20 goals in a year at Sturm Graz before returning to Italy. He was 21 when Genoa signed him for £6million. It should have been the perfect homecoming but the club then owned by 777 Partners plunged into financial chaos.

Relegated from Serie A they were unable to pay wages and Yeboah was loaned to three different clubs in three different countries before finding stability in Minnesota. He has 36 MLS goals in 79 appearances.
